subject: GPU allocation surge — Acme Retail incident response & executive update
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 08:14:23 +0000
Subject: URGENT: SEV-1 — GPU allocation spike impacting eu-dedicated pools (Acme Retail)

Team —

We just received multiple alerts and Acme is reporting sustained errors and high latencies from their dedicated EU cluster. Symptoms: long queuing, repeated preemption/eviction logs from the autoscaler, and token-generation timeouts.

Current ask:
- Marcus & Mina: stand up a triage bridge now, prioritize kernel/allocator traces and the autoscaler controller logs.
- Monica: open line with Acme execs — we need an immediate customer-facing note with impact and ETA.
- Marissa: loop Sales/AE for contractual escalation and potential credits.

I'll open the bridge and post links to logs. This looks like an autoscaler race that is causing GPUs to repeatedly attach/detach under burst load.

Diego
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: bridge-logs-18may.txt (excerpt)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 08:22:10 +0000
Subject: Re: URGENT: SEV-1 — GPU allocation spike impacting eu-dedicated pools (Acme Retail)

Diego / team —

On it; bridge (Zoom: redwood.inc/bridge-3421) is up and I have engineers pulling kernel traces and controller logs. Early signal: race in the scale-up path where multiple allocators attempt to bind the same device group; that causes transient detach+reattach which kicks KV caches out and spikes latency. I'm asking infra to pin the autoscaler to the last stable commit while we iterate a hotfix.

Immediate mitigation plan (T-minus):
- 08:30: pin autoscaler to stable commit (Marcus)
- 08:40: drain and stabilize 2 affected hosts to restore healthy capacity (Infra)
- 09:00: deploy hotfix branch with mutex for allocator binding (Marcus/Mina)
- 09:30: validate end-to-end with staged traffic for Acme only (Monica)

I'll post logs and a short summary in the bridge.

— Marcus
Sr. Infra Engineer

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@acmeretail.com>, Tom Fletcher <tfletcher@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:05:02 +0000
Subject: Customer update: current impact & remediation steps (Acme Retail)

Samira / Tom —

Thank you for your patience — quick executive update on the situation and what to expect in the next 2 hours.

What happened:
- Around 08:05 UTC we observed a rapid increase in concurrent requests to your dedicated EU pool. Our autoscaling controller experienced a race condition under this burst that caused GPUs to be repeatedly detached and reattached. That led to sustained queuing and several token-generation timeouts for a subset of requests.

Impact:
- Intermittent request failures and elevated latency for request arriving between ~08:05–09:05 UTC. Approx. 18% of requests saw >5s latency and 6% returned 5xx. No data loss; KV cache re-warms caused higher token cost.

What we did so far:
- Immediate mitigation: pinned autoscaler to last stable release (08:30 UTC) and drained the two affected hosts to restore capacity.
- Hotfix: engineering is deploying a mutex-based allocator fix and will validate under staged traffic targeted to your tenant only.
- We opened a prioritized Bridge and shared logs.

Next steps & ETA:
- 09:00 UTC: hotfix rollout to EU-dedicated (targeted)
- 09:30 UTC: validation and gradual reintroduction of full traffic
- 10:00 UTC: expected normalization for the majority of requests; we'll continue to monitor for 24h.

Why this matters:
- We recognize the service disruption impacts your user experience and product SLAs. We are treating this as SEV-1 and will provide a post-incident report with root cause, timeline, and compensatory options.

Attachments: acme_exec_note_v1.pdf (summary slide for execs)

I'll be on the bridge and will push updates every 30 minutes or when we have major milestones.

Diego Fernandez
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-555-0192

From: Samira Khan <samira.k@acmeretail.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Fletcher <tfletcher@acmeretail.com>, Acme IT <it-leads@acmeretail.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:18:47 +0000
Subject: Re: Customer update: current impact & remediation steps (Acme Retail)

Diego —

Thanks for the quick update and for setting expectations. We appreciate the targeted rollback and hotfix effort. A couple of asks from our side:
- Confirm whether any customer traffic was processed with partial responses (we want to understand potential downstream user impact).
- We need a single point of contact for billing/credits conversations (our procurement will require a formal statement).

Tom and I will stay on the bridge for validation. Please flag immediately if you see any abnormal state after the rollout.

Samira
VP Product, Acme Retail

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:02:57 +0000
Subject: Post-incident: follow-ups, short RCA and next steps

Team —

Hotfix deployed at 09:05 UTC and staged validation completed by 09:28 UTC. By 09:40 UTC we saw latency return to baseline and error rates drop to normal. Acme traffic was fully reintroduced at 09:50 UTC.

Immediate follow-ups (owners):
- Root cause RCA write-up (Mina) — draft by EOD 2027-05-19
- Compensatory proposal for Acme (Monica + Sales) — draft to Samira by morning EOD 2027-05-19
- Long-term mitigation: autoscaler controller redesign (Marcus) — RFC due 2027-06-02
- Log retention and correlation artifacts uploaded to incident folder (Diego) — done (link below)

Public-facing summary (for customer): short executive note + timeline and proposed credits. I'll include a timeline of events and a patch summary in the RCA.

Links: https://redwood-internal.incidents/INC-20270518 (internal incident page)
Jira: https://jira.redwood.com/PROJECTS/SUP-4281

— Mina
Reliability Lead

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 18:02:10 +0000
Subject: RE: Post-incident: follow-ups, short RCA and next steps

Thanks all — closing the customer-facing loop:
- Sent the final exec note and timeline to Samira this afternoon at 15:30 UTC (see attachment acme_exec_note_v1.pdf).
- Monica & Marissa: please sync on the compensatory draft and send to Acme legal/procurement. Work with finance for any credits; flag if we need leadership approval.
- Mina & Marcus: great job on the hotfix; please include test vectors that exercise allocator concurrency in the RCA.

I'll update the incident page with the postmortem link once the RCA draft is ready.

Diego
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
